title: In the image (Genesis 1:26–27)
hook: every person is made in God's image; the rabbis say a king's coins look alike, but God's people never do (Mishnah Sanhedrin 4:5)

segments.voice: Yesterday: yom, the day. Three days of rooms, three days of filling them. Your line was count the good.

Take two coins of the same kind. Same face on both, a president or a queen, down to the last line of the hair. That's the point of a coin: stamped from one die, identical, interchangeable. Nobody cares which quarter they get. Now think of any ten people. Not one of them is the same. Nearly two thousand years ago, the rabbis put those two facts side by side, and made them one of the boldest teachings in Jewish law.
screen: `TWO COINS, THE SAME FACE.` → `TEN PEOPLE, NO TWO ALIKE.` → `THE RABBIS PUT THEM TOGETHER.`

segments.voice: On the sixth day, the Torah slows down. In the Jewish Publication Society's 1917 translation: "And God created man in His own image, in the image of God created He him; male and female created He them." In Hebrew: tzelem Elohim. Tzelem is an image, a likeness, the word for a statue or a figure. Elohim is God. Every human being carries God's likeness. What that likeness is, the Torah doesn't say. Maimonides said the mind, the ability to understand. Others say freedom, the power to choose, or to create, or to love. Now the coins. The Mishnah, describing how judges warned witnesses in a capital case, puts it this way. A human king stamps many coins with one seal, and they all look alike. The King of kings stamped every person with the seal of the first human, and not one is like another. God's image makes us different, not the same. Then it goes further. Why was humanity created from a single person? So that whoever destroys one life is as if they destroyed a whole world, and whoever saves one life, as if they saved a whole world. So no one can say to anyone else, my ancestor was greater than yours. And so each person is obliged to say: the world was created for my sake. Two rabbis once argued over the Torah's greatest principle. Rabbi Akiva said: love your neighbor as yourself. Ben Azzai pointed to the verse about humanity made in God's likeness, and said his was greater, because it covers everyone.
screen: `TZELEM ELOHIM — THE IMAGE OF GOD.` · `WHAT IS THE IMAGE? IT DOESN'T SAY.` · `ONE SEAL, NO TWO ALIKE.` · `ONE LIFE IS A WHOLE WORLD.` · then, large: `IN THE IMAGE OF GOD CREATED HE HIM.`

segments.voice: Picture a face you passed recently and barely noticed: a cashier, a driver, someone on the street. See it clearly, down to the one detail that's theirs and nobody else's. If you believe what the verse says, see God's image there; if you don't, see one entire world.
Tzelem Elohim. The image of God, stamped on every person, so that no two are alike.
Your line: no two faces alike. One seal, and every face its own. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Jewish teaching and law draw on tzelem Elohim for the dignity of every person, from the care of the sick to the honor given to the dead; the Mishnah's saying about saving one life as saving a whole world is widely quoted.

fork.setup: the Mishnah asks: why was humanity created from just one person? which answer does it give?
options: so the world would fill slowly.
so that one life counts as a whole world.
so there would be one family name.
fork.reveal: whoever destroys one life destroys a world; whoever saves one saves a world. and no one can say their ancestor was greater.

original.note: Hebrew: the image of God. tzelem is the word for a likeness or figure.

trapdoor: what you thought: people look like God.
what it means: every person carries God's likeness, and that likeness makes each one different, and each one a whole world.
what a scholar hears: Mishnah Sanhedrin 4:5 turns the coin image into law for witnesses; Maimonides (Guide 1:1) reads the image as intellect; Ben Azzai calls Genesis 5:1 the Torah's great principle.
